difficultyReason: Historical/scientific stimulus with a modest entailed inference. Traps overreach by adding causal language or extending the claim beyond what the passage supports.
stimulus: Penicillin was discovered by Alexander Fleming in 1928 when he observed that a mold, Penicillium notatum, had contaminated one of his bacterial cultures and was inhibiting bacterial growth around it. Fleming published his findings but did not pursue the clinical development of the substance. It was not until the early 1940s, when Howard Florey and Ernst Chain developed techniques to purify and mass-produce penicillin, that the drug became available for widespread medical use. The delay between Fleming's discovery and the drug's clinical availability spanned more than a decade.
questionStem: Which one of the following can be properly inferred from the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Fleming's failure to develop penicillin clinically was the sole reason the drug was unavailable for more than a decade after its discovery.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Before the 1940s, no researcher other than Fleming had attempted to develop a substance derived from Penicillium notatum.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Penicillin was not widely available for medical use at the time Fleming first published his findings about it.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Florey and Chain's purification techniques were superior to any method that could have been employed in the 1920s.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Fleming recognized that penicillin would eventually become the most important antibiotic in medical history.

explanations.correct: Fleming published findings in 1928, but widespread clinical availability did not come until the early 1940s following Florey and Chain's work. Therefore, when Fleming published, the drug was not yet widely available — this is directly entailed by the timeline the passage establishes.
explanations.A: Too strong / overreach — the passage says Fleming did not pursue development, but does not establish this as the sole reason for the delay. Other technical or resource barriers could have contributed.
explanations.B: Scope overreach — the passage does not state that no other researcher attempted work on the substance; it only describes what Fleming, Florey, and Chain did.
explanations.C: Correct. The passage states widespread use came only after early-1940s development, placing Fleming's 1928 publication well before clinical availability.
explanations.D: Too strong — the passage does not compare Florey and Chain's methods to all possible 1920s methods, only noting that their techniques enabled mass production.
explanations.E: Overreach — the passage makes no claim about Fleming's own predictions or beliefs regarding penicillin's historical significance.

difficultyReason: Conditional-logic stimulus with two linked rules. The correct answer requires chaining the conditionals; traps reverse the direction or commit scope shifts.
stimulus: A municipal ordinance governing building permits states the following: any structure that exceeds four stories in height must have a sprinkler system installed throughout. Any structure with a sprinkler system installed must also have its sprinkler system inspected annually by a licensed fire-safety engineer. The Harlow Tower is a newly constructed building that exceeds four stories in height.
questionStem: If the statements above are true, which one of the following must also be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Any building that has its sprinkler system inspected annually must exceed four stories in height.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Harlow Tower must have its sprinkler system inspected annually by a licensed fire-safety engineer.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Buildings that do not exceed four stories are not required to have annual fire-safety inspections of any kind.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Harlow Tower's fire-safety engineer must also be qualified to approve building permits.

choices.label: E
choices.text: A building with a sprinkler system that has never been inspected must be fewer than four stories tall.

explanations.correct: Harlow Tower exceeds four stories → must have sprinklers (rule 1). Has sprinklers → must be inspected annually by a licensed fire-safety engineer (rule 2). Chaining these two conditionals entails B.
explanations.A: Reversal trap — the conditional runs from 'exceeds four stories' to 'needs sprinklers' to 'needs inspection,' not the reverse. Having inspections does not entail height.
explanations.B: Correct. Two-step conditional chain from Harlow Tower's height to required annual inspection.
explanations.C: Scope shift — the ordinance covers buildings exceeding four stories but says nothing about what shorter buildings are or are not required to do regarding other inspection types.
explanations.D: Overreach — the passage says nothing about permit-approval qualifications for fire-safety engineers.
explanations.E: Reversal and overreach — lacking inspection does not tell us the building's height; the passage establishes what is required, not what violations imply about height.

difficultyReason: Economic/policy stimulus with numerical and comparative facts. Correct answer is a modest hedged inference; traps add causal or absolute language not found in the passage.
stimulus: A government subsidy program distributed grants to small farms in Region X during the three-year period from 2018 to 2020. Records show that the total number of operating small farms in Region X was higher at the end of 2020 than at the beginning of 2018. During the same period, the number of small farms that received no subsidy payment declined each year. The program's administrators noted that some farms receiving subsidies still ceased operations before 2020 ended.
questionStem: Which one of the following must also be true on the basis of the statements above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The subsidy program was the primary cause of the increase in the number of operating small farms in Region X.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Every small farm that received a subsidy payment remained in operation through the end of 2020.

choices.label: C
choices.text: At least some small farms that received subsidy payments were still operating at the end of 2020.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The number of small farms receiving subsidies increased each year from 2018 to 2020.

choices.label: E
choices.text: No small farm in Region X ceased operations during the period from 2018 to 2020.

explanations.correct: The total number of operating farms was higher at end of 2020 than at the start of 2018. The passage also confirms some subsidized farms ceased operations before 2020 ended — but the net count still rose. This means at minimum some subsidized farms (and likely others) remained operating. More directly: the total count of operating farms increased, and since some subsidized farms did close, the ones still operating must include at least some that received subsidies (or that total could not have grown as described). Either way, the net increase entails that at least some farms — including some that received subsidies — were operating at end of 2020.
explanations.A: Causal overreach — the passage establishes correlation between the program and farm counts but does not identify the subsidy as the primary cause.
explanations.B: Too strong — the passage explicitly states some subsidized farms ceased operations before 2020 ended, directly contradicting B.
explanations.C: Correct. The net increase in farms combined with the fact that operations were ongoing entails that at least some subsidized farms survived to 2020.
explanations.D: Overreach — the passage says the number of non-subsidized farms declined each year, but does not directly state that subsidized farm counts rose each year.
explanations.E: Contradicted by the stimulus — the passage notes that some subsidized farms ceased operations during this period.

difficultyReason: Environmental science stimulus with comparative and hedged claims. Correct answer reflects a modest entailment; traps introduce absolute language or unwarranted causal claims.
stimulus: Researchers studying deforestation in a tropical region found that between 1990 and 2010 the total area of old-growth forest decreased by 34 percent. During the same period, the region's human population increased substantially. The researchers also found that areas located within 20 kilometers of a road had significantly higher rates of deforestation than areas more than 20 kilometers from any road. Some portions of the old-growth forest that remained in 2010 were located more than 20 kilometers from the nearest road.
questionStem: Which one of the following can be properly inferred from the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Population growth was the primary driver of deforestation in the region between 1990 and 2010.

choices.label: B
choices.text: All old-growth forest that was deforested between 1990 and 2010 was located within 20 kilometers of a road.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Not all of the old-growth forest present in 1990 had been eliminated by 2010.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The construction of new roads was the only factor that led to increased deforestation rates near existing roads.

choices.label: E
choices.text: If road construction in the region had been halted after 1990, deforestation would not have occurred.

explanations.correct: The passage states that some portions of old-growth forest remained in 2010. This directly entails that not all of it had been eliminated — a straightforward inference from 'some remained.'
explanations.A: Causal overreach — the passage notes population increase and road proximity as correlates but does not identify population growth as the primary driver.
explanations.B: Too strong — the passage says areas near roads had higher deforestation rates, not that deforestation occurred only near roads.
explanations.C: Correct. The passage explicitly states some old-growth forest remained in 2010, which entails that not all of it was eliminated.
explanations.D: Causal overreach — the passage identifies road proximity as a correlate of higher deforestation rates but does not establish road construction as the only factor.
explanations.E: Counterfactual overreach — the passage does not support any claim about what would have happened under different road-construction scenarios.

difficultyReason: Linguistics/cognitive science stimulus with comparative descriptive claims. The correct answer is a modest inference from the comparative data; traps add mechanisms or absolutes not in the passage.
stimulus: Studies of bilingual speakers have found that individuals who learned their second language before the age of seven tend to process both languages in overlapping regions of the brain, while those who learned a second language after age twelve tend to process the two languages in more spatially distinct brain regions. Neuroimaging data also show that bilingual speakers who learned a second language in early childhood display shorter response times on tasks requiring them to switch between languages than do late learners of a second language.
questionStem: If the statements above are true, which one of the following must also be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Learning a second language before age seven is the only way to achieve native-level fluency in that language.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The spatial overlap in brain regions observed in early learners is the cause of their shorter language-switching response times.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Not all bilingual speakers process their two languages in the same way in the brain.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Late learners of a second language are incapable of processing both languages fluently.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Individuals who learned a second language between ages seven and twelve process languages identically to those who learned before age seven.

explanations.correct: The passage describes two distinct groups — early learners (before age 7) and late learners (after age 12) — who process their languages in neurologically different ways. This directly entails that not all bilingual speakers process their two languages the same way.
explanations.A: Overreach — the passage says nothing about fluency levels or native-level proficiency.
explanations.B: Causal overreach — the passage notes both the overlap and the shorter response times in early learners but does not establish the overlap as the cause of the response-time difference.
explanations.C: Correct. Two distinct processing patterns are described for different groups of bilinguals, which entails that not all bilinguals process languages identically.
explanations.D: Too strong — the passage describes processing differences, not inability to achieve fluency.
explanations.E: Scope shift — the passage discusses learners before age 7 and after age 12 but makes no claim about the 7–12 group, so this cannot be inferred.

difficultyReason: Ethics/policy stimulus describing a committee's findings. Correct inference is hedged and modest; traps introduce normative claims or extend findings beyond the stated scope.
stimulus: A professional ethics committee reviewed 200 cases in which medical practitioners had been accused of failing to obtain informed consent from patients. The committee found that in 140 of the 200 cases, the practitioner had provided written information about the procedure but had not verbally confirmed the patient's understanding before proceeding. In the remaining 60 cases, neither written information nor verbal confirmation was provided. The committee concluded its report without issuing any recommendations regarding penalties.
questionStem: Which one of the following must also be true on the basis of the statements above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The majority of the cases reviewed involved practitioners who provided some written information to patients.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Practitioners who provided written information were found by the committee to have acted ethically.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The committee determined that verbal confirmation alone is sufficient to constitute informed consent.

choices.label: D
choices.text: All 200 practitioners reviewed by the committee were ultimately penalized for their conduct.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Written information and verbal confirmation together are always sufficient to establish informed consent.

explanations.correct: 140 out of 200 cases involved practitioners who provided written information. 140 is 70 percent of 200, which is a majority. This is a straightforward numerical inference directly entailed by the passage.
explanations.A: Correct. 140 of 200 = 70%, which is by definition a majority.
explanations.B: Contradicted by the stimulus — all 200 cases were reviewed as accusations of failing to obtain informed consent, meaning providing written information alone was not deemed sufficient; it does not imply ethical conduct.
explanations.C: Overreach — the passage describes what practitioners did or did not do, not what the committee determined to be sufficient for informed consent.
explanations.D: Contradicted by the stimulus — the passage explicitly states the committee concluded without issuing any recommendations regarding penalties.
explanations.E: Overreach — the passage does not address what combination of steps is always sufficient to establish informed consent.

difficultyReason: Technology/history stimulus in a descriptive register similar to the Quebec Bridge anchor. Correct answer is a modest, hedged entailment; traps overreach with absolute claims about intent or cause.
stimulus: The first commercially operated electric power grid, built by Thomas Edison in New York City, began service in 1882. It used direct current (DC) to supply electricity to a small number of customers within roughly one mile of the generating station, because DC loses voltage rapidly over long distances. Within a decade, alternating current (AC) systems championed by George Westinghouse and Nikola Tesla had demonstrated the ability to transmit electricity over distances far exceeding one mile without comparable voltage loss. By the mid-1890s, AC transmission had become the dominant technology for long-distance electrical distribution in the United States.
questionStem: Which one of the following can be properly inferred from the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Edison's DC grid was deliberately designed to prevent competitors from developing long-distance transmission technology.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The first commercial electric power grid was capable of serving customers located more than one mile from its generating station.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Alternating current systems had no technical limitations that affected their practical deployment.

choices.label: D
choices.text: At the time Edison's grid began service, AC transmission systems were not yet in commercial operation.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Edison recognized that alternating current would eventually supplant direct current for long-distance transmission.

explanations.correct: Edison's DC grid began service in 1882. AC systems demonstrated long-distance capability within a decade and became dominant by the mid-1890s. The passage implies AC commercial operation came after 1882, entailing that AC systems were not yet commercially operating when Edison's grid launched.
explanations.A: Intent overreach — the passage describes technical limitations of DC but attributes no competitive intent to Edison's design choices.
explanations.B: Contradicted by the stimulus — the passage explicitly states the grid supplied electricity to customers within roughly one mile of the station, with DC's voltage loss over distance being the limiting factor.
explanations.C: Too strong — the passage does not state that AC had no limitations, only that it transmitted over longer distances without comparable voltage loss.
explanations.D: Correct. The timeline places DC's 1882 commercial launch before AC systems demonstrated long-distance capability 'within a decade,' entailing AC was not yet commercially operating in 1882.
explanations.E: Intent overreach — the passage makes no claim about Edison's beliefs or predictions regarding the future of AC technology.

difficultyReason: Arts/cultural history stimulus with comparative and descriptive facts. The correct answer requires a modest temporal inference; traps introduce evaluative claims or absolute generalizations not in the passage.
stimulus: The Impressionist movement in painting emerged in France during the 1860s and 1870s, characterized in part by the use of short, visible brushstrokes and an emphasis on capturing the effects of light at specific moments. The Académie des Beaux-Arts, the official arbiter of artistic standards in France at the time, repeatedly rejected Impressionist works for its annual Salon exhibition during the movement's early years. Several Impressionist painters subsequently organized their own independent exhibitions beginning in 1874. These independent exhibitions attracted significant public attention, though critical reception in the mainstream French press was initially mixed.
questionStem: Which one of the following must also be true on the basis of the statements above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Académie des Beaux-Arts eventually reversed its position and accepted Impressionist works into the Salon.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Impressionist paintings were universally condemned by French art critics during the 1870s.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The independent Impressionist exhibitions beginning in 1874 were organized at least in part because official exhibition venues had rejected these artists' works.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Académie des Beaux-Arts was the only institution in France with authority to determine which artworks could be publicly displayed.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Impressionist painters received no recognition of any kind prior to the first independent exhibition in 1874.

explanations.correct: The passage states that the Académie repeatedly rejected Impressionist works from the Salon, and that Impressionist painters subsequently organized their own independent exhibitions. The word 'subsequently' places the independent exhibitions as a response to the rejections, entailing that the rejections were at least part of the motivation for organizing independent shows.
explanations.A: Overreach — the passage does not describe any reversal by the Académie; it only describes rejections during the movement's early years.
explanations.B: Too strong — the passage says critical reception in the mainstream press was 'mixed,' explicitly ruling out universal condemnation.
explanations.C: Correct. The sequence — repeated rejection by the Académie followed by the organization of independent exhibitions — entails that the rejections were at least part of the reason for the independent shows.
explanations.D: Scope overreach — the passage identifies the Académie as the 'official arbiter' but does not state it was the only institution with any authority over public display.
explanations.E: Too strong — the passage does not say Impressionists received no recognition before 1874; it describes the Salon rejections and the subsequent exhibitions without cataloguing all recognition they may have received.

difficultyReason: Law/policy stimulus with conditional rule statements and a specific case. Correct answer chains two rules; traps reverse the conditionals or add unsupported normative claims.
stimulus: Under the evidentiary rules of a particular jurisdiction, any statement made by a party outside of court proceedings is classified as hearsay if it is offered in court to prove the truth of the matter asserted. Hearsay statements are inadmissible as evidence unless they fall within a recognized exception. One recognized exception permits the admission of statements made by a party who is unavailable to testify at trial, provided those statements were against the declarant's financial interest at the time they were made. At a recent civil trial, a statement made outside court by the plaintiff, who died before trial, was offered to prove the truth of the matter it asserted.
questionStem: If the statements above are true, which one of the following must also be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The plaintiff's statement is admissible in evidence because the plaintiff is unavailable to testify.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The plaintiff's statement constitutes hearsay under the jurisdiction's evidentiary rules.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The plaintiff's statement is inadmissible regardless of any other facts about the statement.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Any statement that is admissible under an exception to hearsay must have been made against the declarant's financial interest.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The jurisdiction's evidentiary rules treat all out-of-court statements as inadmissible.

explanations.correct: The passage defines hearsay as any out-of-court statement offered to prove the truth of the matter asserted. The plaintiff's statement was made outside court and was offered to prove the truth of what it asserted. Both conditions of the definition are met, so it must be classified as hearsay.
explanations.A: Too strong — unavailability is only one condition of the exception; the statement also must have been against the declarant's financial interest. Since we do not know whether that condition is met, admissibility cannot be established.
explanations.B: Correct. The definition of hearsay is fully satisfied: the statement was made outside court and offered to prove the truth of the matter asserted.
explanations.C: Too strong — the passage identifies exceptions that could render the statement admissible. Without knowing whether an exception applies, inadmissibility cannot be declared absolute.
explanations.D: Scope overreach — the passage describes one recognized exception involving financial interest, but does not state it is the only exception, so this cannot apply to all admissible hearsay exceptions.
explanations.E: Contradicted by the stimulus — the passage states hearsay is inadmissible unless an exception applies, implying some out-of-court statements are admissible under exceptions.

difficultyReason: Environmental science/policy stimulus with comparative statistical data. The correct answer is a modest quantitative inference; traps introduce causal claims or extend findings to populations not described.
stimulus: A regional water authority tested drinking water samples from 150 municipal wells in a predominantly agricultural county. Of those wells, 90 showed detectable levels of nitrate contamination above the threshold established by federal health guidelines. The authority's report noted that all 90 contaminated wells were located within two kilometers of active agricultural fields that had received synthetic fertilizer applications in the preceding year. The remaining 60 wells, none of which exceeded the federal threshold, were all located more than two kilometers from such fields.
questionStem: Which one of the following can be properly inferred from the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Synthetic fertilizer applications were the direct cause of nitrate contamination in all 90 affected wells.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Wells located more than two kilometers from fertilized fields will never show nitrate contamination above federal thresholds.

choices.label: C
choices.text: More than half of the wells tested showed nitrate contamination above the federal health guideline threshold.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The federal health guideline threshold for nitrate is set at a level that prevents all adverse health effects from nitrate exposure.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The water authority concluded that synthetic fertilizer use should be restricted within two kilometers of municipal wells.

explanations.correct: 90 of 150 wells tested showed contamination above the federal threshold. 90 out of 150 equals 60 percent, which is more than half. This is a direct numerical inference from the figures stated in the passage.
explanations.A: Causal overreach — the passage establishes a geographic correlation between proximity to fertilized fields and contamination, but does not establish synthetic fertilizers as the direct cause of the contamination.
explanations.B: Too strong — the passage reports that the 60 non-contaminated wells tested were more than two kilometers away, but does not license a universal claim about all future or untested wells at that distance.
explanations.C: Correct. 90/150 = 60%, which is more than half, directly entailed by the numerical data in the passage.
explanations.D: Overreach — the passage references the federal threshold as a measurement benchmark but makes no claim about what health effects the threshold is designed to prevent.
explanations.E: Overreach — the passage describes the authority's testing and findings but does not state that the authority issued any policy recommendation regarding fertilizer use restrictions.
